reason: E1 directly states that strength arises from fluctuations of shear-fault energy and links SRO to these fluctuations and wavy dislocations. E3 explicitly shows that LCO (SRO) heightens energy landscape ruggedness and raises activation barriers governing dislocation activities, and that processing conditions change LCO and fault energies. E2 supports that CCAs exhibit local chemical ordering and fault energy fluctuations after thermal processing. Together, the cited evidence accurately supports all key premises.
premises: Fluctuations in local shear-fault energy, not the average value, govern strength in CCAs
Local chemical short-range ordering (SRO) produces spatial fluctuations of planar fault energy
SRO heightens the ruggedness of the energy landscape and raises activation barriers for dislocations
Dislocations in CCAs with SRO are distinctively wavy, affecting strength
SRO and its effects on fault energies can be controlled by alloy processing conditions
